cards.tl:
Ko amar Adonai kol b'ramah nishma n'hi b'chi tamrurim Rachel m'vakah al baneha mei-anah l'hinacheim al baneha ki einenu
Ko amar Adonai min'i koleich mibechi v'einayich midim'ah ki yeish sachar lif'ulateich n'um Adonai v'shavu mei-eretz oyeiv

cards.he: קוֹל בְּרָמָה נִשְׁמָע נְהִי בְּכִי תַמְרוּרִים רָחֵל מְבַכָּה עַל־בָּנֶיהָ
cards.tl: Kol b'ramah nishma n'hi b'chi tamrurim Rachel m'vakah al baneha
cards.gloss: "A cry is heard in Ramah... Rachel weeping for her children. She refuses to be comforted" (Jeremiah 31:15). God doesn't scold her. God answers: "Restrain your voice from weeping... They shall return from the enemy's land" (31:16).

cards.q: In Jeremiah 31, how does God answer Rachel's weeping?
choices: With a promise that her children will return
By telling her to stop grieving
cards.why: "**They shall return** from the enemy's land."
wrong_why: God says to restrain her tears, but because of the promise that follows.
God answers her directly.

cards.body: The Talmud has **Jeremiah 31**, the chapter with Rachel's weeping, as a **Rosh Hashanah haftarah** (Megillah 31a). Check what CBB reads.

cards.prompt: Rachel refuses to be comforted, and God answers with hope instead of correction. What does that say to you about grief? It's fine to skip this one.

points: Rachel dies **on the road**, giving birth to Benjamin.
Rashi: buried there to **weep for her children** in exile.
**A cry is heard in Ramah**: Rachel refuses comfort (Jeremiah 31:15).
God's answer: **they shall return**.
Jeremiah 31 is a **Rosh Hashanah** haftarah (Megillah 31a).

lessons.title: Jacob (7): Wrestling until dawn
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Rashi on Genesis 32:8, 32:11, 32:25 and 32:29 (read on Sefaria 11/10).

cards.title: Alone at night
cards.body: Twenty years after the stolen blessing, Jacob is about to meet **Esau** again. He is afraid. He prays, sends everyone across the river, and is **left alone**. A figure wrestles with him **until dawn** (32:8-25).

cards.q: What new name does Jacob receive that night?
cards.why: **Israel**, "for you have striven with beings divine and human, and have prevailed" (32:29).

cards.title: Two fears
cards.body: "Jacob was greatly frightened; in his anxiety..." (32:8). Why two words? **Rashi**: he was afraid **he would be killed**, and distressed that **he might have to kill** someone.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב אֱלֹהֵי אָבִי אַבְרָהָם וֵאלֹהֵי אָבִי יִצְחָק יְיָ הָאֹמֵר אֵלַי שׁוּב לְאַרְצְךָ וּלְמוֹלַדְתְּךָ וְאֵיטִיבָה עִמָּךְ
קָטֹנְתִּי מִכֹּל הַחֲסָדִים וּמִכׇּל־הָאֱמֶת אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתָ אֶת־עַבְדֶּךָ כִּי בְמַקְלִי עָבַרְתִּי אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּן הַזֶּה וְעַתָּה הָיִיתִי לִשְׁנֵי מַחֲנוֹת
cards.en: Then Jacob said, “O God of my father Abraham’s [house] and God of my father Isaac’s [house], O יהוה, who said to me, ‘Return to your native land and I will deal bountifully with you’! I am unworthy of all the kindness that You have so steadfastly shown Your servant: with my staff alone I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer Yaakov Elohei avi Avraham v'Elohei avi Yitzchak Adonai ha-omeir eilai shuv l'artz'cha ul'moladt'cha v'eitivah imach
Katonti mikol hachasadim umikol ha-emet asher asita et avdecha ki v'makli avarti et hayardein hazeh v'atah hayiti lishnei machanot

cards.he: קָטֹנְתִּי מִכֹּל הַחֲסָדִים וּמִכׇּל־הָאֱמֶת
cards.tl: Katonti mikol hachasadim umikol ha-emet
cards.gloss: "I am unworthy of all the kindness that You have so steadfastly shown Your servant" (32:11). **Rashi**: my merits are **diminished** by all the kindness You have already shown me.

cards.q: In Rashi's reading of 32:8, what was Jacob's second fear?
choices: That he might have to kill someone
That Esau would take his flocks
cards.why: Afraid of **being killed**, and distressed at the thought of **killing**.
wrong_why: Rashi says nothing about the flocks here.
Rachel isn't part of Rashi's reading.

cards.he:
וַיִּוָּתֵר יַעֲקֹב לְבַדּוֹ וַיֵּאָבֵק אִישׁ עִמּוֹ עַד עֲלוֹת הַשָּׁחַר
וַיַּרְא כִּי לֹא יָכֹל לוֹ וַיִּגַּע בְּכַף־יְרֵכוֹ וַתֵּקַע כַּף־יֶרֶךְ יַעֲקֹב בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ עִמּוֹ
וַיֹּאמֶר שַׁלְּחֵנִי כִּי עָלָה הַשָּׁחַר וַיֹּאמֶר לֹא אֲשַׁלֵּחֲךָ כִּי אִם־בֵּרַכְתָּנִי
cards.en: Jacob was left alone. And a figure wrestled with him until the break of dawn. When he saw that he had not prevailed against him, he wrenched Jacob’s hip at its socket, so that the socket of his hip was strained as he wrestled with him. Then he said, “Let me go, for dawn is breaking.” But he answered, “I will not let you go, unless you bless me.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayivateir Yaakov l'vado vayei-aveik ish imo ad alot hashachar
Vayar ki lo yachol lo vayiga b'chaf y'reicho vateika kaf yerech Yaakov b'hei-avko imo
Vayomer shal'cheini ki alah hashachar vayomer lo ashaleichacha ki im beirachtani

cards.title: Who was the figure?
cards.body: The Torah says only **"a figure"** (in Hebrew, a man). **Rashi**: the Rabbis explained he was **Esau's guardian angel**. By morning Jacob says he has seen **a divine being face to face** (32:31).

cards.he: לֹא אֲשַׁלֵּחֲךָ כִּי אִם־בֵּרַכְתָּנִי
cards.tl: Lo ashaleichacha ki im beirachtani
cards.gloss: "I will not let you go, unless you bless me" (32:27). Wounded at the hip, Jacob **holds on**.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו מַה־שְּׁמֶךָ וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב
וַיֹּאמֶר לֹא יַעֲקֹב יֵאָמֵר עוֹד שִׁמְךָ כִּי אִם־יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי־שָׂרִיתָ עִם־אֱלֹהִים וְעִם־אֲנָשִׁים וַתּוּכָל
וַיִּשְׁאַל יַעֲקֹב וַיֹּאמֶר הַגִּידָה־נָּא שְׁמֶךָ וַיֹּאמֶר לָמָּה זֶּה תִּשְׁאַל לִשְׁמִי וַיְבָרֶךְ אֹתוֹ שָׁם
cards.en: Said the other, “What is your name?” He replied, “Jacob.” Said he, “Your name shall no longer be Jacob, but Israel, for you have striven with beings divine and human, and have prevailed.” Jacob asked, “Pray tell me your name.” But he said, “You must not ask my name!” And he took leave of him there.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer eilav ma sh'mecha vayomer Yaakov
Vayomer lo Yaakov yei-ameir od shimcha ki im Yisrael ki sarita im Elohim v'im anashim vatuchol
Vayish'al Yaakov vayomer hagidah na sh'mecha vayomer lamah zeh tish'al lishmi vay'varech oto sham

cards.he: כִּי אִם־יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי־שָׂרִיתָ עִם־אֱלֹהִים וְעִם־אֲנָשִׁים וַתּוּכָל
cards.tl: Ki im Yisrael ki sarita im Elohim v'im anashim vatuchol
cards.gloss: "...but Israel, for you have striven with beings divine and human, and have prevailed" (32:29). **Rashi**: no longer will it be said that the blessings came to you **by supplanting**, but by **noble conduct**, in the open.

cards.q: According to Rashi, what does the change from Jacob to Israel mean?
choices: His blessings now come openly, not by supplanting
He is forbidden to use the name Jacob
cards.why: **Yaakov** echoes the heel and supplanting; **Yisrael**, striving and prevailing in the open.
wrong_why: Rashi doesn't speak of kingship.
The Torah keeps calling him Jacob too; Rashi's point is how his blessings are earned.

cards.title: Limping into the sunrise
cards.body: Jacob names the place **Peniel**: "I have seen a divine being face to face, yet my life has been preserved." Then "the sun rose upon him" as he passed, **limping on his hip** (32:31-32).
Every time you say **Sh'ma Yisrael**, you use the name Jacob earned that night.

cards.prompt: Jacob won't let go until he's blessed, and walks away limping. Is there a struggle you've come through changed? It's fine to skip this one.

points: Rashi 32:8: afraid **to be killed**, and **to kill**.
"**I am unworthy** of all the kindness" (32:11).
A figure, Rashi: **Esau's guardian angel**.
"**I will not let you go, unless you bless me.**"
**Israel**: blessings won in the open (Rashi 32:29); Jacob limps into the sunrise.

lessons.title: Jacob (8): Esau runs to meet him
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Rashi on Genesis 33:4 (from Bereshit Rabbah 78:8 and Sifrei Bamidbar 69), read on Sefaria 11/10. The dots over vayishakehu are in Sefaria's Masorah text.

cards.title: Four hundred men
cards.body: Jacob sees **Esau coming with four hundred men**. He places his family in rows, **Rachel and Joseph last**, walks ahead, and **bows to the ground seven times** (33:1-3).

cards.q: When they meet, Esau attacks Jacob.
cards.why: "Esau **ran** to greet him. He **embraced** him and, falling on his neck, he **kissed** him; and **they wept**" (33:4).

cards.he:
וַיִּשָּׂא יַעֲקֹב עֵינָיו וַיַּרְא וְהִנֵּה עֵשָׂו בָּא וְעִמּוֹ אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת אִישׁ וַיַּחַץ אֶת־הַיְלָדִים עַל־לֵאָה וְעַל־רָחֵל וְעַל שְׁתֵּי הַשְּׁפָחוֹת
וַיָּשֶׂם אֶת־הַשְּׁפָחוֹת וְאֶת־יַלְדֵיהֶן רִאשֹׁנָה וְאֶת־לֵאָה וִילָדֶיהָ אַחֲרֹנִים וְאֶת־רָחֵל וְאֶת־יוֹסֵף אַחֲרֹנִים
וְהוּא עָבַר לִפְנֵיהֶם וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ אַרְצָה שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים עַד־גִּשְׁתּוֹ עַד־אָחִיו
וַיָּרׇץ עֵשָׂו לִקְרָאתוֹ וַיְחַבְּקֵהוּ וַיִּפֹּל עַל־צַוָּארָו וַׄיִּׄשָּׁׄקֵׄהׄוּׄ וַיִּבְכּוּ
cards.en: Looking up, Jacob saw Esau coming, with a retinue of four hundred. He divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two maids, putting the maids and their children first, Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph last. He himself went on ahead and bowed low to the ground seven times until he was near his brother. Esau ran to greet him. He embraced him and, falling on his neck, he kissed him; and they wept.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayisa Yaakov einav vayar v'hinei eisav ba v'imo arba mei-ot ish vayachatz et hayladim al Leah v'al Rachel v'al sh'tei hash'fachot
Vayasem et hash'fachot v'et yaldeihen rishonah v'et Leah viladeha acharonim v'et Rachel v'et yoseif acharonim
V'hu avar lifneihem vayishtachu artzah sheva p'amim ad gishto ad achiv
Vayarotz eisav likrato vaychab'keihu vayipol al tzavarav vayishakeihu vayivku
Vayishakeihu
cards.gloss: "he kissed him" (33:4). In the Masoretic text this word carries **dots over its letters**. **Rashi**: the sages disagreed. Some say Esau **did not kiss him wholeheartedly**. **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai**: Esau hated Jacob, but at that moment his **pity was truly aroused**, and he kissed him **with his whole heart**.

cards.q: What does Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai learn from the dots over "he kissed him"?
choices: At that moment Esau kissed him with his whole heart
cards.why: Despite the old hatred, **in that moment** Esau's pity was real.
wrong_why: That's the other opinion Rashi reports.
No one suggests erasing it; the dots invite interpretation.

cards.title: Why he embraced him
cards.body: **Rashi**: Esau's pity was aroused when he saw Jacob **bowing to the ground so many times**. Seven bows, and a twenty-year grudge gives way.

cards.he: וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב אַל־נָא אִם־נָא מָצָאתִי חֵן בְּעֵינֶיךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ מִנְחָתִי מִיָּדִי כִּי עַל־כֵּן רָאִיתִי פָנֶיךָ כִּרְאֹת פְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים וַתִּרְצֵנִי
cards.en: But Jacob said, “No, I pray you; if you would do me this favor, accept from me this gift; for to see your face is like seeing the face of God, and you have received me favorably.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vayomer Yaakov al na im na matzati chein b'einecha v'lakachta minchati miyadi ki al kein ra-iti fanecha kir'ot p'nei Elohim vatirtzeini

cards.he: רָאִיתִי פָנֶיךָ כִּרְאֹת פְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים
cards.tl: Ra-iti fanecha kir'ot p'nei Elohim
cards.gloss: "to see your face is like seeing the face of God" (33:10). The night before, Jacob saw a divine being **face to face** (32:31). Now he sees God in **his brother's face**.

cards.q: What does Jacob tell Esau seeing his face is like?
cards.why: "To see your face is like **seeing the face of God**" (33:10).
wrong_why: Isaac isn't mentioned here.
Not in the text.

cards.prompt: Twenty years after the stolen blessing, Esau runs to his brother. What do you think made this meeting possible?

points: Jacob bows **seven times**; Esau **runs** to him.
Dots over "he kissed him": Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, **with his whole heart** (Rashi 33:4).
Esau's pity was aroused by Jacob's bowing.
"To see your face is like seeing **the face of God**."

lessons.title: Joseph (1): The tunic, the dreams and the pit
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Rashi on Genesis 37:15, 37:24 and 37:35 (read on Sefaria 11/11). 'Coat of many colours' is the King James rendering.

cards.title: The favorite son
cards.body: "Israel loved Joseph best of all his sons" and gave him **an ornamented tunic**. His brothers **hated him**, and then Joseph told them **his dreams** (37:3-7).

cards.q: "The pit was empty; there was no water in it" (37:24). According to Rashi, what was in it?
cards.why: Why add "no water" if it was empty? **Rashi**: no water, but **snakes and scorpions**.

cards.he:
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אָהַב אֶת־יוֹסֵף מִכׇּל־בָּנָיו כִּי־בֶן־זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ וְעָשָׂה לוֹ כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים
וַיִּרְאוּ אֶחָיו כִּי־אֹתוֹ אָהַב אֲבִיהֶם מִכׇּל־אֶחָיו וַיִּשְׂנְאוּ אֹתוֹ וְלֹא יָכְלוּ דַּבְּרוֹ לְשָׁלֹם
cards.en: Now Israel loved Joseph best of all his sons—he was his “child of old age”; and he had made him an ornamented tunic. And when his brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of his brothers, they hated him so that they could not speak a friendly word to him.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
V'Yisrael ahav et yoseif mikol banav ki ven z'kunim hu lo v'asah lo k'tonet pasim
Vayir'u echav ki oto ahav avihem mikol echav vayisn'u oto v'lo yachlu dab'ro l'shalom

cards.he: כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים
cards.tl: K'tonet pasim
cards.gloss: "an ornamented tunic" (37:3). The rare Hebrew word for its decoration has been translated many ways; the King James Bible made it the famous "coat of many colours."

cards.he:
וַיַּחֲלֹם יוֹסֵף חֲלוֹם וַיַּגֵּד לְאֶחָיו וַיּוֹסִפוּ עוֹד שְׂנֹא אֹתוֹ
וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם שִׁמְעוּ־נָא הַחֲלוֹם הַזֶּה אֲשֶׁר חָלָמְתִּי
וְהִנֵּה אֲנַחְנוּ מְאַלְּמִים אֲלֻמִּים בְּתוֹךְ הַשָּׂדֶה וְהִנֵּה קָמָה אֲלֻמָּתִי וְגַם־נִצָּבָה וְהִנֵּה תְסֻבֶּינָה אֲלֻמֹּתֵיכֶם וַתִּשְׁתַּחֲוֶיןָ לַאֲלֻמָּתִי
cards.en: Once Joseph had a dream which he told to his brothers; and they hated him even more. He said to them, “Hear this dream which I have dreamed: There we were binding sheaves in the field, when suddenly my sheaf stood up and remained upright; then your sheaves gathered around and bowed low to my sheaf.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayachalom yoseif chalom vayageid l'echav vayosifu od s'no oto
Vayomer aleihem shim'u na hachalom hazeh asher chalamti
V'hinei anachnu m'al'mim alumim b'toch hasadeh v'hinei kamah alumati v'gam nitzavah v'hinei t'subenah alumoteichem vatishtachavena la-alumati

cards.title: The man in the field
cards.body: On his way to his brothers, "a man came upon him wandering in the fields" (37:15). An ordinary stranger? **Rashi**: this was **the angel Gabriel**.

cards.he: אֶת־אַחַי אָנֹכִי מְבַקֵּשׁ
cards.tl: Et achai anochi m'vakeish
cards.gloss: "I am looking for my brothers" (37:16): said by the boy his brothers hate, on his way to find them.

cards.q: Who does Rashi say the "man" in the field was?
cards.why: **Gabriel**: a hidden messenger who keeps the story moving.
wrong_why: The brothers were already gone to Dothan.
That's the plain reading; Rashi brings the midrash.

cards.he:
וַיְהִי כַּאֲשֶׁר־בָּא יוֹסֵף אֶל־אֶחָיו וַיַּפְשִׁיטוּ אֶת־יוֹסֵף אֶת־כֻּתׇּנְתּוֹ אֶת־כְּתֹנֶת הַפַּסִּים אֲשֶׁר עָלָיו
וַיִּקָּחֻהוּ וַיַּשְׁלִכוּ אֹתוֹ הַבֹּרָה וְהַבּוֹר רֵק אֵין בּוֹ מָיִם
cards.en: When Joseph came up to his brothers, they stripped Joseph of his tunic, the ornamented tunic that he was wearing, and took him and cast him into the pit. The pit was empty; there was no water in it.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vay'hi ka-asher ba yoseif el echav vayafshitu et yoseif et kutonto et k'tonet hapasim asher alav
Vayikachuhu vayashlichu oto haborah v'habor reik ein bo mayim

cards.title: Empty, but not empty
cards.body: "The pit was **empty**; there was **no water** in it." Why say both? **Rashi**, from the Talmud: there was no water, but there were **snakes and scorpions**.

cards.he:
וַיִּקְרַע יַעֲקֹב שִׂמְלֹתָיו וַיָּשֶׂם שַׂק בְּמׇתְנָיו וַיִּתְאַבֵּל עַל־בְּנוֹ יָמִים רַבִּים
וַיָּקֻמוּ כׇל־בָּנָיו וְכׇל־בְּנֹתָיו לְנַחֲמוֹ וַיְמָאֵן לְהִתְנַחֵם וַיֹּאמֶר כִּי־אֵרֵד אֶל־בְּנִי אָבֵל שְׁאֹלָה וַיֵּבְךְּ אֹתוֹ אָבִיו
cards.en: Jacob rent his clothes, put sackcloth on his loins, and observed mourning for his son many days. All his sons and daughters sought to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted, saying, “No, I will go down mourning to my son in Sheol.” Thus his father bewailed him.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayikra Yaakov simlotav vayasem sak b'motnav vayit'abeil al b'no yamim rabim
Vayakumu chol banav v'chol b'notav l'nachamo vayma-ein l'hitnacheim vayomer ki eireid el b'ni aveil sh'olah vayeivk oto aviv

cards.title: He refused to be comforted
cards.body: Jacob mourns and **refuses to be comforted** (37:35). **Rashi**: no one can be comforted over someone **still alive** who is thought dead. It is decreed that the dead are slowly forgotten from the heart, but not the living. Joseph is alive.

cards.q: Why, in Rashi's reading, could Jacob not be comforted?
choices: He blamed himself for the tunic
cards.why: Comfort comes for **the dead**, who fade from the heart. Joseph was **alive**.
wrong_why: "All his sons and daughters sought to comfort him" (37:35).
Rashi gives a different reason.

points: A favorite son, **an ornamented tunic**, and dreams.
Rashi: the man in the field was **Gabriel**.
"**I am looking for my brothers.**"
The pit: no water, but **snakes and scorpions** (Rashi).
Jacob **refuses comfort**: Joseph is alive (Rashi 37:35).

lessons.title: Joseph (2): Adonai was with Joseph
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Rashi on Genesis 39:3 (from Tanchuma) and Sotah 36b (cited by Rashi on 39:11), read on Sefaria 11/11.

cards.title: A slave in Egypt
cards.body: Sold by his brothers, Joseph becomes a slave in the house of Potiphar, an Egyptian official. Yet the Torah says, "Adonai was with Joseph" (39:2).

cards.q: Joseph's Egyptian master could tell that God was with him.
cards.why: "His master saw that Adonai was with him" (39:3). Rashi explains **how** he could see it.

cards.he:
וַיְהִי יְיָ אֶת־יוֹסֵף וַיְהִי אִישׁ מַצְלִיחַ וַיְהִי בְּבֵית אֲדֹנָיו הַמִּצְרִי
וַיַּרְא אֲדֹנָיו כִּי יְיָ אִתּוֹ וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר־הוּא עֹשֶׂה יְיָ מַצְלִיחַ בְּיָדוֹ
cards.en: יהוה was with Joseph, and he was a successful man; and he stayed in the house of his Egyptian master. And when his master saw that יהוה was with him and that יהוה lent success to everything he undertook,
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vay'hi Adonai et yoseif vay'hi ish matzliach vay'hi b'veit adonav hamitzri
Vayar adonav ki Adonai ito v'chol asher hu oseh Adonai matzliach b'yado

cards.title: God's name in his mouth
cards.body: How could an Egyptian **see** that God was with Joseph? **Rashi**: the name of God was **always on his lips**. God's presence showed in how Joseph spoke and acted.

cards.q: According to Rashi, how did Potiphar see that God was with Joseph?
choices: God's name was always on Joseph's lips
Joseph told him about his dreams
cards.why: Not miracles: **Joseph's own speech** made God visible.
wrong_why: The Torah describes no miracles here.
The dreams aren't part of Rashi's answer.

cards.he:
וַיְמָאֵן וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל־אֵשֶׁת אֲדֹנָיו הֵן אֲדֹנִי לֹא־יָדַע אִתִּי מַה־בַּבָּיִת וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר־יֶשׁ־לוֹ נָתַן בְּיָדִי
אֵינֶנּוּ גָדוֹל בַּבַּיִת הַזֶּה מִמֶּנִּי וְלֹא־חָשַׂךְ מִמֶּנִּי מְאוּמָה כִּי אִם־אוֹתָךְ בַּאֲשֶׁר אַתְּ־אִשְׁתּוֹ וְאֵיךְ אֶעֱשֶׂה הָרָעָה הַגְּדֹלָה הַזֹּאת וְחָטָאתִי לֵאלֹהִים
cards.en: But he refused. He said to his master’s wife, “Look, with me here, my master gives no thought to anything in this house, and all that he owns he has placed in my hands. He wields no more authority in this house than I, and he has withheld nothing from me except yourself, since you are his wife. How then could I do this most wicked thing, and sin before God?”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayma-ein vayomer el eishet adonav hein adoni lo yada iti ma babayit v'chol asher yesh lo natan b'yadi
Einenu gadol babayit hazeh mimeni v'lo chasach mimeni m'umah ki im otach ba-asher at ishto v'eich e-eseh hara-ah hag'dolah hazot v'chatati leilohim

cards.title: His father's face
cards.body: Potiphar's wife tries again and again to seduce Joseph. The Talmud: at the moment of greatest temptation, **his father's image appeared to him in the window**, and reminded him of **his place among his brothers**. Joseph fled.

cards.q: In Sotah 36b, what helped Joseph resist?
choices: His father's image appeared to him
cards.why: **Jacob's face**, and the memory of who Joseph was meant to be.
wrong_why: The Talmud's answer is more inward than that.
His own words (39:9) are about loyalty and sin, not fear.

cards.he: וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵלָיו חֲלוֹם חָלַמְנוּ וּפֹתֵר אֵין אֹתוֹ וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵהֶם יוֹסֵף הֲלוֹא לֵאלֹהִים פִּתְרֹנִים סַפְּרוּ־נָא לִי
cards.en: And they said to him, “We had dreams, and there is no one to interpret them.” So Joseph said to them, “Surely God can interpret! Tell me [your dreams].”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vayomru eilav chalom chalamnu ufoteir ein oto vayomer aleihem yoseif halo leilohim pitronim sap'ru na li

cards.he: הֲלוֹא לֵאלֹהִים פִּתְרֹנִים
cards.tl: Halo leilohim pitronim
cards.gloss: "Surely God can interpret!" (40:8). In prison, Joseph gives the credit away before he even hears the dreams.

cards.prompt: Joseph is a slave, then a prisoner, and still the Torah says God was with him. In this story, where does God's presence actually show up?

points: "**Adonai was with Joseph**," even as a slave.
Rashi: God's name was **always on his lips**.
Sotah 36b: **his father's face** in the window.
"**Surely God can interpret!**"

lessons.title: Joseph (3): Pharaoh's dreams
lessons.check_note: Torah text only, plus the custom of blessing children with Ephraim and Manasseh (Genesis 48:20).

cards.title: From prison to palace
cards.body: Pharaoh dreams of **seven fat cows and seven lean ones**, and no one can explain it. Joseph is brought **straight from prison** (41:1-15).

cards.q: Pharaoh says Joseph can interpret any dream. What does Joseph answer?
choices: "Not I! God will see to Pharaoh's welfare."
cards.why: "**Not I!**" (41:16). Again Joseph points away from himself.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר פַּרְעֹה אֶל־יוֹסֵף חֲלוֹם חָלַמְתִּי וּפֹתֵר אֵין אֹתוֹ וַאֲנִי שָׁמַעְתִּי עָלֶיךָ לֵאמֹר תִּשְׁמַע חֲלוֹם לִפְתֹּר אֹתוֹ
וַיַּעַן יוֹסֵף אֶת־פַּרְעֹה לֵאמֹר בִּלְעָדָי אֱלֹהִים יַעֲנֶה אֶת־שְׁלוֹם פַּרְעֹה
cards.en: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have had a dream, but no one can interpret it. Now I have heard it said of you that for you to hear a dream is to tell its meaning.” Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, “Not I! God will see to Pharaoh’s welfare.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer par'o el yoseif chalom chalamti ufoteir ein oto va-ani shamati alecha leimor tishma chalom liftor oto
Vaya-an yoseif et par'o leimor bil'adai Elohim ya-aneh et sh'lom par'o

cards.he: בִּלְעָדָי אֱלֹהִים יַעֲנֶה אֶת־שְׁלוֹם פַּרְעֹה
cards.tl: Bil'adai Elohim ya-aneh et sh'lom par'o
cards.gloss: "Not I! God will see to Pharaoh's welfare" (41:16). Before he names God, Joseph answers in **a single Hebrew word**.

cards.he:
וַיִּקְרָא יוֹסֵף אֶת־שֵׁם הַבְּכוֹר מְנַשֶּׁה כִּי־נַשַּׁנִי אֱלֹהִים אֶת־כׇּל־עֲמָלִי וְאֵת כׇּל־בֵּית אָבִי
וְאֵת שֵׁם הַשֵּׁנִי קָרָא אֶפְרָיִם כִּי־הִפְרַנִי אֱלֹהִים בְּאֶרֶץ עׇנְיִי
cards.en: Joseph named the first-born Manasseh, meaning, “God has made me forget completely my hardship and my parental home.” And the second he named Ephraim, meaning, “God has made me fertile in the land of my affliction.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayikra yoseif et sheim hab'chor m'nasheh ki nashani Elohim et kol amali v'eit kol beit avi
V'eit sheim hasheini kara efrayim ki hifrani Elohim b'eretz onyi

cards.title: Two names
cards.body: Joseph names his sons **Manasseh**, "God has made me forget completely my hardship," and **Ephraim**, "God has made me fertile in the land of my affliction" (41:51-52). Jacob later blesses them, and Jewish parents still bless their sons on Friday night to be like **Ephraim and Manasseh** (48:20).

cards.q: What does the name Ephraim say?
choices: God made me fertile in the land of my affliction
God made me forget my father's house
God made me ruler over Egypt
cards.why: **Ephraim**: fruitful **in the land of affliction** (41:52).
wrong_why: That's Manasseh's name.
Neither name says that.

cards.prompt: Ephraim: "fertile in the land of my affliction." Has anything grown for you in a hard place? It's fine to skip this one.

points: Joseph goes **from prison to Pharaoh**.
"**Not I!** God will see to Pharaoh's welfare."
**Manasseh** and **Ephraim**: forgetting hardship, and growing in it.
Children are still blessed **to be like Ephraim and Manasseh**.

lessons.title: Joseph (4): The brothers and Judah
lessons.check_note: Rambam, Mishneh Torah, Repentance 2:1 (Touger translation on Sefaria), read 11/11. The observation that Genesis 37 records no plea from Joseph is from the text itself.

cards.title: Bowing to a stranger
cards.body: Famine drives Joseph's brothers to Egypt. They **bow** to the governor, as in Joseph's dream. Joseph recognizes them; **they do not recognize him** (42:6-8).

cards.q: When the brothers come to Egypt, they recognize Joseph.
cards.why: Joseph **recognized them**, but **they did not recognize him** (42:8).

cards.he: וַיֹּאמְרוּ אִישׁ אֶל־אָחִיו אֲבָל אֲשֵׁמִים אֲנַחְנוּ עַל־אָחִינוּ אֲשֶׁר רָאִינוּ צָרַת נַפְשׁוֹ בְּהִתְחַנְנוֹ אֵלֵינוּ וְלֹא שָׁמָעְנוּ עַל־כֵּן בָּאָה אֵלֵינוּ הַצָּרָה הַזֹּאת
cards.en: They said to one another, “Alas, we are being punished on account of our brother, because we looked on at his anguish, yet paid no heed as he pleaded with us. That is why this distress has come upon us.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vayomru ish el achiv aval asheimim anachnu al achinu asher ra-inu tzarat nafsho b'hitchan'no eileinu v'lo shamanu al kein ba-ah eileinu hatzarah hazot

cards.title: We looked on at his anguish
cards.body: Years later, the brothers say they **watched his anguish** and ignored him **as he pleaded** (42:21). Chapter 37 never mentions Joseph pleading. We hear his cry only now, **through their guilt**.

cards.q: What do we first learn in 42:21 that chapter 37 didn't tell us?
choices: Joseph pleaded with his brothers from the pit
cards.why: The plea is told **only in memory**, when the brothers' guilt surfaces.
wrong_why: There's no third dream.
Reuben wanted to save him (37:22).

cards.he:
וְעַתָּה יֵשֶׁב־נָא עַבְדְּךָ תַּחַת הַנַּעַר עֶבֶד לַאדֹנִי וְהַנַּעַר יַעַל עִם־אֶחָיו
כִּי־אֵיךְ אֶעֱלֶה אֶל־אָבִי וְהַנַּעַר אֵינֶנּוּ אִתִּי פֶּן אֶרְאֶה בָרָע אֲשֶׁר יִמְצָא אֶת־אָבִי
cards.en: Therefore, please let your servant remain as a slave to my lord instead of the boy, and let the boy go back with his brothers. For how can I go back to my father unless the boy is with me? Let me not be witness to the woe that would overtake my father!”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
V'atah yeishev na avd'cha tachat hana-ar eved ladoni v'hana-ar ya-al im echav
Ki eich e-eleh el avi v'hana-ar einenu iti pen er'eh vara asher yimtza et avi

cards.title: Complete teshuvah
cards.body: Long ago, **Judah** proposed selling Joseph (37:26-27). Now Joseph tests them with Benjamin, Rachel's other son, and Judah offers to **stay as a slave in his place** (44:33). **Rambam**: complete teshuvah is when you face **the same situation** again and choose differently, not out of fear or weakness.

cards.q: Why is Judah's offer a model of complete teshuvah, in Rambam's terms?
choices: He faces the same situation and chooses differently
cards.why: Same test, a brother at risk, and **this time he protects him**.
wrong_why: Rambam asks for more than words.
Gifts aren't the measure here.

points: The brothers **bow**, and don't recognize Joseph.
Joseph's plea from the pit is heard **only in their guilt** (42:21).
**Judah** offers himself for Benjamin.
Rambam: complete teshuvah is choosing differently **in the same situation**.

lessons.title: Joseph (5): I am Joseph
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Bereshit Rabbah 93:10 and Zohar, Miketz 11:182 (Soncino translation on Sefaria), read 11/11.

cards.title: He could no longer hold back
cards.body: Judah's plea breaks Joseph open. He sends everyone else out and says: "I am Joseph. Is my father still well?" (45:1-3).

cards.q: After "I am Joseph," what does Joseph ask first?
cards.why: His first question is about **his father** (45:3).

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר יוֹסֵף אֶל־אֶחָיו אֲנִי יוֹסֵף הַעוֹד אָבִי חָי וְלֹא־יָכְלוּ אֶחָיו לַעֲנוֹת אֹתוֹ כִּי נִבְהֲלוּ מִפָּנָיו
וַיֹּאמֶר יוֹסֵף אֶל־אֶחָיו גְּשׁוּ־נָא אֵלַי וַיִּגָּשׁוּ וַיֹּאמֶר אֲנִי יוֹסֵף אֲחִיכֶם אֲשֶׁר־מְכַרְתֶּם אֹתִי מִצְרָיְמָה
וְעַתָּה אַל־תֵּעָצְבוּ וְאַל־יִחַר בְּעֵינֵיכֶם כִּי־מְכַרְתֶּם אֹתִי הֵנָּה כִּי לְמִחְיָה שְׁלָחַנִי אֱלֹהִים לִפְנֵיכֶם
cards.en: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph. Is my father still well?” But his brothers could not answer him, so dumbfounded were they on account of him. Then Joseph said to his brothers, “Come forward to me.” And when they came forward, he said, “I am your brother Joseph, he whom you sold into Egypt. Now, do not be distressed or reproach yourselves because you sold me hither; it was to save life that God sent me ahead of you.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer yoseif el echav ani yoseif ha-od avi chai v'lo yachlu echav la-anot oto ki nivhalu mipanav
Vayomer yoseif el echav g'shu na eilai vayigashu vayomer ani yoseif achichem asher m'chartem oti mitzraymah
V'atah al tei-atzvu v'al yichar b'eineichem ki m'chartem oti heinah ki l'michyah sh'lachani Elohim lifneichem

cards.title: The day of rebuke
cards.body: "His brothers could not answer him." **Abba Kohen Bardela**: woe to us on **the day of rebuke**. Joseph was the youngest, and his brothers **could not withstand his rebuke**. How much more, when **God** comes to rebuke each person **according to who they are**.

cards.q: What does Abba Kohen Bardela learn from the brothers' silence?
choices: If they couldn't face Joseph, how much harder to face God's judgment
cards.why: "I am Joseph" was rebuke enough. **The day of judgment** will be harder.
wrong_why: The midrash isn't about language.
The midrash reads the silence as shame, not mishearing.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵהֶם יוֹסֵף אַל־תִּירָאוּ כִּי הֲתַחַת אֱלֹהִים אָנִי
וְאַתֶּם חֲשַׁבְתֶּם עָלַי רָעָה אֱלֹהִים חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטֹבָה לְמַעַן עֲשֹׂה כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה לְהַחֲיֹת עַם־רָב
cards.en: But Joseph said to them, “Have no fear! Am I a substitute for God? Besides, although you intended me harm, God intended it for good, so as to bring about the present result—the survival of many people.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer aleihem yoseif al tira-u ki hatachat Elohim ani
V'atem chashavtem alai ra-ah Elohim chashavah l'tovah l'ma-an aso kayom hazeh l'hachayot am rav

cards.he: וְאַתֶּם חֲשַׁבְתֶּם עָלַי רָעָה אֱלֹהִים חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטֹבָה
cards.tl: V'atem chashavtem alai ra-ah Elohim chashavah l'tovah
cards.gloss: "although you intended me harm, God intended it for good" (50:20). After Jacob dies, the brothers fear revenge. Joseph answers: "Have no fear! Am I a substitute for God?"

cards.title: Not repaying evil
cards.body: The **Zohar** holds up "Joseph the righteous" as the model of one who **does not repay evil**: when his brothers fell into his hands, he told himself, "wait for the Lord, and he will save thee" (Proverbs 20:22).

cards.q: Why does the Zohar call Joseph "the righteous" here?
choices: He had his brothers in his power and did not repay evil
cards.why: Power over those who hurt him, and **he chose not to use it**.
wrong_why: The Zohar's point here is restraint, not dreams.
Power alone isn't righteousness; how he used it is.

cards.prompt: Joseph says God meant it for good, but it's Joseph who chooses to forgive. Where do you see God in that choice?

points: "**I am Joseph.** Is my father still well?"
Bereshit Rabbah 93:10: **the day of rebuke**.
"You intended me harm, **God intended it for good**."
Zohar: Joseph the righteous **did not repay evil**.

units.title: Holiday stories
units.subtitle: The stories behind Shavuot, Hanukkah and Yom Kippur afternoon

lessons.title: Ruth: The stranger who stayed
lessons.check_note: My retelling of Ruth 1-4 and Leviticus 19:9-10; quotes are paraphrased. Check most closely: Ruth Rabbah 2:14 (purpose of the book) and the Shavuot traditions. Does CBB read Ruth on Shavuot?

cards.title: Three widows
cards.body: A famine drives **Elimelech and Naomi** from Bethlehem to **Moab**, an old rival nation. Their sons marry Moabite women, **Orpah and Ruth**. Then all three men die, leaving three widows with no one to support them.

cards.q: Naomi tells both daughters-in-law to go back to their mothers' homes. What does Ruth do?
choices: Asks Naomi to stay in Moab
cards.why: Ruth **refuses to leave**. Naomi's people will be her people, and Naomi's God her God.

cards.title: Where you go, I will go
cards.body: Orpah kisses Naomi goodbye. Ruth holds on. Wherever Naomi goes and wherever she sleeps, Ruth will too; **Naomi's people will be her people and Naomi's God her God**, and only death will part them.

cards.he:
וַתֹּאמֶר רוּת אַל־תִּפְגְּעִי־בִי לְעׇזְבֵךְ לָשׁוּב מֵאַחֲרָיִךְ כִּי אֶל־אֲשֶׁר תֵּלְכִי אֵלֵךְ וּבַאֲשֶׁר תָּלִינִי אָלִין עַמֵּךְ עַמִּי וֵאלֹהַיִךְ אֱלֹהָֽי׃
בַּאֲשֶׁר תָּמוּתִי אָמוּת וְשָׁם אֶקָּבֵר כֹּה יַעֲשֶׂה יְיָ לִי וְכֹה יוֹסִיף כִּי הַמָּוֶת יַפְרִיד בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵֽךְ׃
cards.en: But Ruth replied, “Do not urge me to leave you, to turn back and not follow you. For wherever you go, I will go; wherever you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God. Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. Thus and more may GOD do to me if anything but death parts me from you.”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl:
Vatomer Rut al tifg'i vi l'ozveich lashuv mei-acharayich ki el asher teilchi eileich uva-asher talini alin ameich ami veilohayich Elohai.
Ba-asher tamuti amut v'sham ekaveir ko ya-aseh Adonai li v'cho yosif ki hamavet yafrid beini uveineich.

cards.title: Gleaning
cards.body: They reach Bethlehem as the **barley harvest** begins. Ruth goes out to **glean**, picking up the grain the reapers leave behind. The Torah tells farmers to leave the edges of the field and the fallen grain **for the poor and the stranger**. Ruth is both.

cards.q: Why could Ruth gather grain in a field that wasn't hers?
choices: The Torah leaves gleanings for the poor and the stranger
Naomi owned part of the field
cards.why: Leaving gleanings is a **Torah law**: the edges and the fallen grain belong to the poor and the stranger.
wrong_why: Boaz only notices her after she is already gleaning. He never hires her.
Naomi came home with nothing. She had no crop.

cards.title: Boaz
cards.body: The field belongs to **Boaz**, a relative of Elimelech. He has heard how Ruth stood by Naomi. He tells her to stay in his field, orders his workers not to bother her, and has them pull out extra stalks for her to gather.

cards.title: The redeemer
cards.body: Naomi sends Ruth to ask Boaz to be her **go'el**, redeemer: the relative who takes responsibility for a family's land and name. A closer relative turns it down and seals it by handing over his sandal. **Boaz marries Ruth.**

cards.he: כִּי גֹאֵל אָתָּה
cards.tl: Ki go-eil atah
cards.gloss: "For you are a **redeemer**" (3:9). Ruth asks Boaz to step in as **go'el**, the relative who takes responsibility for the family.

cards.q: What was a go'el, a redeemer, in Ruth's world?
choices: A relative who takes responsibility for a family's land and name
cards.why: The go'el is a **relative** who steps in for a family that has lost its men.
wrong_why: Boaz settles it at the town gate in front of elders, but as a relative, not as a judge.
No priest appears anywhere in the book.

cards.title: Great-grandmother of a king
cards.body: Their son is **Obed**, the father of Jesse, the father of **King David**. The book ends with a family tree: Israel's greatest king descends from a woman of Moab.

cards.q: Who is Ruth's great-grandson?
cards.why: Obed, then Jesse, then **David**.
wrong_why: Solomon is David's son, one generation further down.
Samuel anoints David as king but isn't related to Ruth.

cards.title: Hesed
cards.body: A midrash asks why this book was written at all, since it teaches no laws. Its answer: **to teach how great the reward is for hesed**, loyal kindness. Ruth shows it to Naomi, and Boaz to Ruth, each going beyond what was required.

cards.he: הֵיטַבְתְּ חַסְדֵּךְ הָאַחֲרוֹן מִן־הָרִאשׁוֹן
cards.tl: Heitavt chasdeich ha-acharon min harishon
cards.gloss: "Your latest **hesed** is greater than your first" (3:10). Boaz praises Ruth's loyal kindness: first to Naomi, now to the whole family.

cards.q: Put the story in order.
items: Famine and the move to Moab
cards.why: Loss, then loyalty, then kindness answered with kindness, then a royal line.

cards.body: Many congregations read Ruth on **Shavuot**. It is a harvest story for a harvest festival, and Ruth's choice to join the Jewish people is often linked to Israel accepting the Torah at Sinai. A tradition also holds that David was born and died on Shavuot.

cards.prompt: Ruth committed before she knew anything would turn out well. Where in your own Jewish life did you choose first and understand later?

points: Three widows; Ruth **won't leave Naomi**.
She **gleans**, a right the Torah gives the poor and the stranger.
Boaz acts as **go'el** and marries her.
Their great-grandson is **King David**.
The midrash: the book teaches **hesed**.

lessons.title: Hanukkah: The rededication
lessons.check_note: Dates follow the usual scholarly reconstruction from 1 Maccabees. 'Hammer' for Maccabee is the common explanation, not certain. Decide whether the app should mention the classical Reform framing (religious freedom).

cards.title: A story outside the Bible
cards.body: Hanukkah's story **isn't in the Hebrew Bible**. It comes from the **books of Maccabees**, written in the 2nd and 1st centuries BCE and left out of the Jewish canon, and from the **Talmud**, centuries later.

src.note: Kept in the Septuagint and Catholic and Orthodox Bibles, not in the Tanakh.

cards.q: What did the first Hanukkah celebrate?
choices: A jar of oil lasting eight days
cards.why: The earliest source celebrates **rededicating the Temple**. The oil story appears centuries later.

cards.body: Judea is ruled by the **Seleucid** Greek kingdom. Many Jews have taken up Greek culture, and Jews argue bitterly among themselves about how far to go.
King **Antiochus IV** bans Shabbat, circumcision and Torah study, and sets up pagan worship in the **Temple in Jerusalem**.

cards.title: Mattathias says no
cards.body: In the village of **Modi'in**, an old priest named **Mattathias** refuses to sacrifice to the king's gods. He and his sons flee to the hills and start a revolt.

cards.q: What started the revolt?
choices: A priest refused to offer a pagan sacrifice
The Temple ran out of oil
cards.why: In Modi'in, **Mattathias refused** to sacrifice to the king's gods.
wrong_why: The oil story is about the end of the war, and it comes from a much later source.
1 Maccabees tells it as a fight over religion, not money.

cards.title: The hammer
cards.body: His son **Judah** leads the fighting and is nicknamed **Maccabee**, usually explained as "the hammer." Against a much larger army, the rebels win back Jerusalem.

src.note: The meaning of Maccabee is uncertain.

cards.body: They purify the Temple, build a new altar and **rededicate** it with eight days of celebration. **Hanukkah** means "dedication."

src.note: 2 Maccabees 10:6 says the eight days were kept like a late Sukkot.

cards.he: חֲנֻכַּת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
cards.tl: Chanukat hamizbeiach
cards.gloss: "The **dedication of the altar**" (Numbers 7:84). The same word names the dedication of the Tabernacle's altar in the Torah. That chapter is the Torah reading during Hanukkah.

cards.q: What does the word Hanukkah mean?
cards.why: It names the **rededication** of the Temple and its altar.
wrong_why: Light is the holiday's symbol, but the word itself means dedication.
The victory made it possible, but the name is about the Temple.

cards.title: The jar of oil
cards.body: Centuries later the **Talmud** asks, "What is Hanukkah?" and tells a new story: one sealed jar of pure oil, enough for one day, **burned for eight**.

cards.q: Where does the story of the oil first appear?
cards.why: The Babylonian **Talmud**, Shabbat 21b.
wrong_why: 1 Maccabees has eight days of celebration but no oil miracle.
Hanukkah happened long after the Torah was written.

cards.title: Not by might
cards.body: The haftarah for Shabbat of Hanukkah answers the war story. The prophet Zechariah sees a golden lampstand and hears: **not by might and not by power, but by My spirit**.

cards.he: וַיַּעַן וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלַי לֵאמֹר זֶה דְּבַר־יְיָ אֶל־זְרֻבָּבֶל לֵאמֹר לֹא בְחַיִל וְלֹא בְכֹחַ כִּי אִם־בְּרוּחִי אָמַר יְיָ צְבָאֽוֹת׃
cards.en: Then he explained to me as follows: “This is the word of GOD to Zerubbabel: Not by might, nor by power, but by My spirit—said GOD of Hosts.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Vaya-an vayomer eilai leimor zeh d'var Adonai el Z'rubavel leimor lo v'chayil v'lo v'choach ki im b'ruchi amar Adonai tz'va-ot.

cards.q: Put the events in order.
cards.why: Persecution, refusal, revolt, victory, rededication.

cards.body: When you light the candles you hold **both stories**: a stubborn fight for the freedom to live as Jews, and a small light that lasts longer than it should. Different generations have leaned on one or the other.

cards.prompt: Which story speaks to you more right now, the fight or the light? Why?

points: The story comes from **Maccabees** and the **Talmud**, not the Bible.
Antiochus IV **banned Jewish practice**; Mattathias refused.
Judah **the Maccabee** retook Jerusalem.
Hanukkah means **dedication**: the Temple, 25 Kislev.
The **oil** story is from the Talmud; the haftarah says **not by might**.

lessons.title: Jonah: The prophet who ran
lessons.check_note: My retelling of Jonah 1-4; quotes are paraphrased. Confirm that Mishkan HaNefesh and CBB read Jonah on Yom Kippur afternoon.

cards.title: The other direction
cards.body: God tells **Jonah** to go to **Nineveh**, capital of Assyria, Israel's enemy, and call out against its evil. Jonah goes down to **Jaffa** and boards a ship sailing the opposite way, to **Tarshish**.

cards.q: Why did Jonah run, by his own account?
choices: He knew God would forgive Nineveh
He was afraid of being killed
He didn't believe God had spoken
cards.why: He says it himself near the end: he knew God was **gracious and compassionate** and would relent.

cards.title: The storm
cards.body: A great storm hits. The sailors pray, each to his own god, and **cast lots**; the lot falls on Jonah, asleep below deck. He tells them to **throw him overboard**. They try rowing to shore first, then do it, and the sea goes calm.

cards.title: The fish
cards.body: God sends a **great fish** to swallow Jonah. He is inside it for three days and three nights, and **he prays**. Then the fish spits him out onto dry land.

cards.q: How did the sailors find out the storm was about Jonah?
choices: Another prophet on board told them
cards.why: They **cast lots**, and the lot fell on Jonah.
wrong_why: He explains himself only after the lot falls on him.
There is no other prophet in the story.

cards.title: Five words
cards.body: God asks a second time, and Jonah goes. His whole message is **five words in Hebrew**: forty more days, and Nineveh will be overturned.

cards.he: וַיָּחֶל יוֹנָה לָבוֹא בָעִיר מַהֲלַךְ יוֹם אֶחָד וַיִּקְרָא וַיֹּאמַר עוֹד אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְנִֽינְוֵה נֶהְפָּֽכֶת׃
cards.en: Jonah started out and made his way into the city the distance of one day’s walk, and proclaimed: “Forty days more, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.license: CC-BY-NC (Sefaria lists 'unknown' for Jonah; same edition as Ruth and Zechariah)
cards.tl: Vayachel Yonah lavo va-ir mahalach yom echad vayikra vayomar od arba-im yom v'Nin'veih nehpachet.

cards.title: A city turns
cards.body: The people believe. **Everyone fasts and wears sackcloth**, from the king down, and the king orders even the **animals** to fast. They turn from violence, and God does not destroy the city.

cards.he: כִּי־שָׁבוּ מִדַּרְכָּם הָרָעָה
cards.tl: Ki shavu midarkam hara-ah
cards.gloss: "They **turned** from their evil way" (3:10). **Shavu**, they turned, comes from the same root as **teshuvah**.

cards.q: Who repents in Nineveh?
choices: Only the people who heard Jonah
cards.why: The king's decree covers **people and animals alike**.
wrong_why: The king leads, but his decree covers the whole city.
The people start it, but the king's decree spreads it to everyone, animals included.

cards.title: Jonah's anger
cards.body: Jonah is furious. This is why he ran, he says: he knew God is **gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in kindness**, and would relent. He is quoting the attributes God revealed to Moses.

cards.q: Why does Jonah's complaint sound familiar?
choices: He quotes God's attributes from Exodus 34
cards.why: He turns God's own words to Moses, **gracious and compassionate**, into a complaint.
wrong_why: The sailors' prayer asks not to be blamed for his death; it has different words.
The king hopes God may relent, but Jonah's words come from Exodus.

cards.title: The plant
cards.body: Jonah sits outside the city to see what will happen. God grows a plant to shade him, then sends a worm to kill it. In the hot sun, Jonah says he would rather die.

cards.title: The last question
cards.body: God answers: you care about a plant you didn't plant or grow. **Should I not care about Nineveh**, with more than 120,000 people who can't tell their right hand from their left, and many animals? The book ends there. **Jonah never answers.**

cards.q: Put the story in order.
cards.why: Flight, storm, prayer, warning, repentance, and a question left open.

cards.body: Jonah is read on **Yom Kippur afternoon**. On the day of teshuvah, turning, you hear about a whole city that turned, and a prophet who found God's mercy hard to accept. All day you also sing the same attributes Jonah quotes.

cards.prompt: The book ends with a question nobody answers. How would you answer in Jonah's place?

points: Jonah **runs** from his mission to Nineveh.
Storm, lots, and **three days in the fish**.
**Five words**, and the whole city repents, animals too.
Jonah is angry that God is **gracious and compassionate** (Exodus 34).
The book ends with **God's question**, unanswered.
